finding.claim: Clone and checkout write through a symlinked parent directory on case-insensitive filesystems, allowing arbitrary file creation or overwrite outside the worktree.
finding.source: Malicious repository tree (symlink 'A' plus directory 'a/') fetched via Repo.clone, or a later checkout/reset of such a commit.
finding.sink: open(target_path, 'wb') in build_file_from_blob at dulwich/index.py:1916, reached from build_index_from_tree at index.py:2246.

trace.note: iter_tree_contents yields symlink 'A' before directory 'a/' in byte order
validate_path only rejects dot-names; 'A' and 'a' pass, no case-collision check
os.path.exists(wt/a) follows symlink 'A' on case-insensitive FS, so makedirs is skipped
only final component is lstat-checked for symlink; parent is not
open('wt/a/pwned.txt','wb') writes through parent symlink into victim dir

finding.guards_checked: validate_path_element_ntfs (index.py:2078-2100) and validate_path_element_hfs (index.py:2124-2144) reject dot-name spellings only, no case-collision check; symlink check at index.py:1904 covers final component only; no lstat of leading components in build_index_from_tree or update_working_tree; _ensure_parent_dir_exists (index.py:2370-2400) also uses os.path.exists. Correct guard exists in stash.py:70-113 (_verify_leading_dirs, CVE-2021-21300) but is not applied on the clone/checkout path. Preconditions: case-insensitive FS (default macOS APFS, Windows NTFS). Single-tree attack does not collide on case-sensitive Linux; multi-commit variant on Linux appears blocked by delete-before-add ordering but unverified. Statically confirmed by reading; not executed (no shell tool; write to /tmp was denied).

finding.claim: Bundle-URI fetch lets a remote-advertised URI make the client request arbitrary http/https hosts and read the full response body with no size cap.
finding.source: Remote-advertised bundle list entry bundle.<id>.uri (relative URIs resolved at bundle_uri.py:233-239).
finding.sink: urllib3 PoolManager GET at bundle_uri.py:278; unbounded response.data read at bundle_uri.py:283.

trace.note: error message echoes URI and parse failure

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restricted to http/https (bundle_uri.py:273-274). No size cap, no host restriction, no redirect limit beyond urllib3 default. Callers at bundle_uri.py:341, 374, 433 are explicit bundle-URI APIs not invoked by clone. Limited reflection via error text. Impact: SSRF-style requests from client and memory exhaustion.

finding.claim: Archive writes raw git tree mode bits into tar headers, so setuid/setgid bits from an untrusted tree survive into the archive.
finding.source: Tree entry mode from an untrusted repository; tree modes are not restricted outside Tree.check() (objects.py:1610-1618).
finding.sink: tar header mode via info.mode = entry.mode at archive.py:207, written by tar.addfile at archive.py:210.

trace.note: tar.addfile writes header with setuid/setgid bits

finding.guards_checked: _is_unsafe_archive_path (archive.py:229) blocks traversal names. Checkout canonicalizes modes via cleanup_mode (index.py:1925) but archive path does not. Impact is limited to a consumer extracting the archive as root.
